status: Development vectors for the FHT 1.0 contract (FHT-Specification#8). No FHT schema is released and no installed toolkit reads FHT in its default path: every expected outcome is derived from the rule text, never from an implementation under test. D3 file-identity expectation acceptance is recorded separately in expectationReviews.
fhtContract: fht.json — the generated FHT 1.0 development schema (specs/005-rna-transcriptome-header/spec.md)
fhtRuleText: conformance/README.md (C1-C3; renamed from the provisional T1-T3 in FHT-Specification#36)
checksumDefinition: base64(SHA-512/256) over the (decompressed) file bytes except the root-level checksum line and its terminator (docs/FORMAT.md R1-R5); written by scripts/make_fht_fixtures.py and cross-checked by scripts/check_fht_fixtures.py

R1.summary: Checksum rule 1: hash the exact file bytes without normalization; for gzip/BGZF input, the decompressed bytes. A line ends at LF, CRLF or a CR not followed by LF.

R2.summary: Checksum rule 2: exactly one root-level checksum line with an unquoted key; spaces only to match root indentation and before the colon; nested checksum properties (such as a derivedFrom parent checksum) stay covered.

R3.summary: Checksum rule 3: exclude that entire line and its terminator; hash every other byte, so changing covered bytes invalidates the checksum.

R4.summary: Checksum rule 4: SHA-512/256 digest in standard padded base64, no prefix; the encoding is canonical (the unused bits are zero) and checksums compare as exact strings.

R5.summary: Header parsing: the checksum line holds only the 44-character value, plain or quoted, with optional spaces; comments, tags, other text, block scalars and continuation lines are invalid.

R6.summary: Header parsing: FHT header lines are UTF-8 without U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029; bytes outside header lines are not decoded.

R7.summary: Header parsing: a FASTA file must not begin with a UTF-8 byte order mark.

R8.summary: Header parsing: no duplicate mapping keys, YAML anchors, aliases or merge keys.

R9.summary: Header parsing: in microdata the first of repeated attributes applies; itemtype and itemprop are space-separated token lists.
R9.notApplicable: R9 is a microdata rule (docs/FORMAT.md: repeated attributes, `itemtype`/`itemprop` token lists) and has no FASTA vector; no FHT microdata reader or writer exists, so issue #8 box 2 keeps it out of this suite. Measured 2026-11-15 with fair-bioheaders 0.11.0: `bioheaders convert <fht file> out.html --to html` exits 1 with 'HTML microdata output is not available for FHT metadata: no reviewed FHT binding exists (FHT-Specification#9)'. The typed-HTML lane is issue #11.

R10.summary: Header parsing: header lines form the leading block before the first FASTA record; a ';~' line after that point, including one from a concatenated file, is invalid; ordinary ';' comments and blank lines may be mixed in around and inside the block.

R11.summary: Header writing (FASTA): header lines should not contain a raw '>' or '@'; writers escape them as \x3E and \x40 in double-quoted YAML scalars, which read back as the same characters.
R11.notApplicable: R11 is a writing recommendation: a raw '>' or '@' keeps the file valid and validators warn; the shared suite likewise has no invalid R11 vector.

R12.summary: Header parsing: YAML metadata is read with YAML 1.2 core-schema types and must read the same under YAML 1.1; explicit tags and plain scalars that the two versions read differently (010, 1_000, 1:30, yes, on, 1e3) are invalid; plain scalars that look like dates or times are strings, as written.

R13.summary: Numbers: a numeric metadata value must be a finite number. YAML .nan, .inf and -.inf make the record invalid.

R14.summary: Links: a value whose schema format is uri should use http or https (ftp, urn, doi and info are also accepted); any other scheme stays schema-valid, but validators warn.
R14.notApplicable: R14 makes validators warn, not reject: an unexpected link scheme is schema-valid. Its valid vector carries "warnings": ["R14"].

R15.summary: Extension fields: from the FHT 1.0 development contract (FR-010), a top-level key matching ^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ may hold any value; every other unknown key and an x- key in a nested object stay invalid.

V1.summary: Schema selection: raw-main selects the reader's **current** schema of that type, with no fallback to an older release. The shared rule text lists the shared publication repository's raw-main URLs; for FHT the citation is the owning development repository's raw-main URL, which V7 places in the opt-in draft lane. What the V1 vectors here turn on is the no-fallback half: a record that states a version other than the contract the citation selects is rejected, not retried against another schema.

V5.summary: Schema selection: any schema value outside the recognized released-schema URLs is FHR, checked against the reader's current FHR schema; a near-miss URL additionally draws the reader's warning (FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools#125). While no release registers FHT, its release-form URLs (an fht w3id URL, an FHT-Specification raw tag) are such values — the V7 draft lane is the owning development repository's raw-main URL only — and V4 unsupported-version begins only when FHT enters schemas/versions.json.
V5.notApplicable: V5 outcomes depend on the record's bytes; no record that is valid against the FHT contract can be FHR-valid (FHT states schemaVersion '1.0', which the current FHR schema rejects, and the required field sets are disjoint), so V5 has no valid side here. V4 is not registered as a rule of this suite at all: with no FHT row in schemas/versions.json there is no citation it can resolve to.

V7.summary: Schema selection: a reader **may** recognise a draft contract cited as the raw-main URL of the development repository that owns the type, only where the user explicitly chose that lane, reading the draft at the revision the reader is built with and warning on every such record; without the choice, V5 governs and the outcome is exactly what it was before V7 existed. V7 is the precondition of this whole suite, not a per-vector outcome: no expected result changes because of it, so it has no valid/invalid pair here. Measured 2026-11-15 with fair-bioheaders 0.11.0 (docs/CI.md): with the lane closed all 72 vectors are invalid as FHR; with it open the 28 valid vectors are accepted and the 44 rejections hold.
V7.notApplicable: V7 is a reader **configuration**, not a per-vector outcome: it decides whether any record in this suite is read as the draft at all, so it cannot have a valid/invalid pair inside one byte-exact suite. The positive selection vector is `fht-fasta-schema-raw-main`; the lane-closed behavior (every record here becomes invalid as FHR under V5) is measured in docs/CI.md's manual named-toolkit lane, and a configuration-dependent expectation needs its own manifest vocabulary — see conformance/README.md, 'The rule this suite cannot carry yet'.

C1.summary: FHT development contract (text in conformance/README.md): the parsed header metadata must validate against fht.json — required fields, enums, patterns, nested cardinality and the closed top level (plus R15 extension keys), and complete supplied BUSCO component counts must sum exactly to total (a separate arithmetic check, not JSON Schema).

C2.summary: FHT development contract (text in conformance/README.md): a record's schema value must be the one URL the FHT draft accepts, this repository's raw-main fht.json (rule V7: a draft never takes a release form; release forms are added at publication). Another type's schema, a release-form or arbitrary URL fails fht.json; it never silently selects the FHT schema.

C3.summary: FHT development contract (text in conformance/README.md): a derivedFrom parent checksum must equal the checksum recomputed over the supplied parent file's bytes, per link; a mismatch is an invalid link (checked-fail), and a parent that was not supplied makes the link unchecked, never verified.

fht-fasta-lf as one gzip member truncated six bytes before its end, inside the CRC-32/ISIZE trailer: the stream is incomplete, so there are no decompressed bytes for R1 to hash and the file is rejected before any checksum comparison.
The value is standard padded base64 of a SHA-256 digest, not of SHA-512/256; exact-string comparison fails.
The value is SHA-512 truncated to 32 bytes and re-encoded; SHA-512/256 is a distinct algorithm, so the exact string differs (and the encoding may not even be canonical).
The final payload character is outside the canonical set AEIMQUYcgkosw048, so a 32-byte digest can never encode to it.

The file begins with a UTF-8 byte order mark; the BOM also removes the ';~' prefix from the first header line.

A ';~' line after the first FASTA record; it is neither ignored nor merged. (The stated checksum is consistent with the bytes, but a reader must reject the shape before the comparison stage, so this vector is classified 'unreachable'.)

A plain integer with a leading zero: YAML 1.1 reads 011 as octal 9, YAML 1.2 reads decimal 11, so the value is ambiguous (the schema cannot see this — only the R12 rule rejects it).
vitalStats.averageTranscriptLength is the YAML .inf: not a finite number (type 'number' alone accepts it, so R13 is the rejection).
An x- key inside the nested taxon object: extension fields are top level only.

vectors.reason: The child's bytes, metadata and self-checksum are all valid, but the cited parent checksum does not equal the checksum recomputed over the supplied parents/parent-genome.fhr.fasta (checked-fail): a verifier must report an invalid link, not treat it as unchecked and not pass it silently.

The link states the genuine digest of parents/parent-genome.fhr.fasta, but the parent the reader holds is parents/parent-genome-subset.fhr.fasta — a second real file, holding a proper subset of those records, with its own computed digest. C3 compares exact strings, so the verdict is checked-fail: not unchecked, not a shape error, and not something to skip. A reader that reports a match has checked that the value is somebody's digest, not that it is this parent's.

The link states the digest of parents/parent-genome.fhr.fasta while the supplied parent is parents/parent-genome-masked.fhr.fasta. The two files carry the same records and the same letters, differing only in the case of one sequence line, the genome title and the masking value that describes it. R1 hashes exact bytes and C3 compares exact strings, so the verdict is checked-fail: case is not a normalization a verifier may apply, and the uppercase and masked copies of a molecule are two files with two digests (measured on real data in pilot #45).

Two parent links, two verdicts: the FHR transcribedFrom checksum recomputes from parents/parent-genome.fhr.fasta (checked-pass) while the FHT filteredFrom checksum does not equal the value recomputed over the supplied valid/fht-fasta-minimal.fht.fasta (checked-fail). parentLink results are per-entry: a passing link in the same file does not mask the failing one, and a verifier must report the mismatched link as invalid (finalized #37 semantics).

expectationReviews.review: Independent clause derivations and SHA-512/256 recomputation were recorded before David Molik accepted the recommendations.
expectationReviews.limitation: Matching proves exact cited parent-file identity only; no biological derivation or extraction is established.
